Resolves #19293

The Workstation now has a browser witness for the focused, non-active tab that survives a real overflow projection. The test selects a live two-tab right header by predicate, adds a third tab through the dock operation, focuses the non-active tab, waits for its contextual actions to settle, and narrows the current viewport. It checks that the focused tab still has a DOM box, focus remains inside its container, and every pre-existing action node remains present. This PR changes only the test.

Evidence: L3 (headless Chrome + Neural Link against the dev-based branch) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-4). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | The same executable stage and assertions were red against pre-fix `dev@7f310afd5d`: focused node absent, no box, focus on body, and contextual actions withdrawn. [Ticket checkpoint](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19293#issuecomment-5849502039). |
| AC-2 | At `90858ff96e`, `WorkstationFocusedTabOverflowNL` passed 1/1. The arm asserts the focused DOM node and real box, `document.activeElement` inside the tab container, and retention of the pre-projection action-id set. |
| AC-3 | The same arm passed alone 1/1 and beside `WorkstationTabOverflowCapNL` 2/2. Its narrowing is computed from the live viewport rather than a fixed width. |
| AC-4 | The stage selects the right-side, non-reveal two-tab header by predicate and reports rejected candidates when none qualifies. |

## Deltas from ticket

The browser witness is a separate spec beside `WorkstationTabOverflowCapNL` so it runs alone without depending on the cap arm's viewport state. The existing host spec remains unchanged.

## Test Evidence

With `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` set to a Brain checkout, both commands passed on macOS headless Chrome:

- `npx playwright test workstation/WorkstationFocusedTabOverflowNL -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs --workers=1` — 1/1.
- `npx playwright test workstation/WorkstationFocusedTabOverflowNL workstation/WorkstationTabOverflowCapNL -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs --workers=1` — 2/2.

The red control is documented in the ticket checkpoint above. The follow-up commit changes JSDoc only; the tested stage and assertions are unchanged. `git diff --check` and the local source-comment archaeology check passed. `agent-preflight` is not hosted in the Engine checkout; the shared baseline runs in CI.

## Post-Merge Validation

None; the browser witness ran on the preceding commit of this branch, and the current head changes only its JSDoc.

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

- **Decision**: Approve
- **Rationale**: This is a test that has to *convict* a build to be worth anything, and the strongest evidence here is that it does. The arm was run red against a named pre-fix commit (`dev@7f310afd5d`) and the observed failures are specific — focused node absent, no box, focus on body, contextual actions withdrawn — which is the opposite of a test written to pass. The ticket's own history records that two peers previously burned a bisect on a *staging* defect that looked like a product regression; this arm answers that by making every staging precondition an assertion with a failure message, and by printing the rejected candidates when no header qualifies. No required actions: the receipt is sha-pinned and I verified the head delta is JSDoc-only, so the tested artifact's behaviour is the proposed head's behaviour. The one real risk is that nothing runs this spec, which is a property of the NL lane rather than of this PR, so it belongs in the record as a watch and not as a demand.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #19293 in full — including its five measured staging facts and its "Where it stopped" section — the single-file diff, the PR body, and the engine's tab/overflow substrate to confirm what the arm is meant to witness. I also diffed the receipt's sha against the proposed head rather than accepting the claim.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** A browser-level arm that stages a real overflow projection against a focused non-active tab and observes what only the DOM can show — a live box, `document.activeElement`, and the presence of contextual action nodes. I expected a new spec to be brittle in at least one of the five ways the ticket already documents, because the ticket documents them as *measured* failure modes, not as style advice.
*   **Patch Verdict:** **matches**, and it discharges the ticket's own open question rather than working around it. The ticket ended with "the app non-reveal headers may need a THIRD tab to stage this at all, since a two-tab header ends with both ids protected and nothing withheld", having failed to produce an overflow control in a two-tab `neo-tab-header-toolbar-5`. This arm adds a third tab through `executeDockOperation({operation: 'addItem'})` and makes the *focused* tab the last one, which is the staging the ticket said was required. All five measured traps are addressed, each with the ticket's own reasoning visible in the assertion messages: the narrowing is computed from `page.viewportSize().width` and asserted to be a real decrease; focus is taken through the raw DOM node and asserted in **both** the document and the worker before any projection; the action baseline is taken only after a *stable* two-equal-reads poll, because an immediate read saw 1 action where 150 ms later there were 6; retention is asserted as set membership (`beforeActions.every(id => …includes(id))`), never equality, because the narrower header legitimately adds nodes; and the widened tab is the focused one, because in-order packing overflows the last tab regardless of its width.
*   **Premise Coherence:** **coheres: verify-before-assert.** The PR's central claim is not "the behaviour works" but "this arm detects the behaviour breaking", and the receipt is a red run against a real pre-fix sha rather than an assertion that one could construct. It also coheres with friction→gold in the way the ticket's scar tissue demands: the staging knowledge is now executable assertions with explanatory messages, so the next attempt inherits a diagnosis instead of a bisect.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — this is the only browser-level witness of a fix whose current carrier is unit arms, and nothing will tell us when it rots.**

`WorkstationFocusedTabOverflowNL` appears in **no** workflow run list, and neither does any other `Workstation*NL` spec, so the 29/29 green on this PR says nothing about this file — which the PR body is honest about, supplying a sha-pinned local receipt instead. That honesty is the right call and I am not asking for a CI registration: standing the NL lane up in CI is a shared-primitive change well outside a one-file test PR, exactly as #577 correctly classified its own Database-level ack. The consequence belongs in the record anyway. #19293's ticket says the unit arms "carry the fix in the meantime", and the five staging facts were each *measured* against an app composition that has already changed once — the ticket's own scar is two peers chasing a staging defect that looked like a regression. So this arm's value decays silently: the app gains or loses a tab, a header predicate stops matching, a dock operation changes shape, and the failure surfaces only to whoever runs this one file by hand, if at all. Worth naming because the mitigation already exists in the file and is worth preserving as a habit: on a staging failure the assertion prints `rejected=${JSON.stringify(rejected)}` with a per-candidate reason (no projected header, no header DOM, zero width, wrong side, reveal class present, wrong button count). That single line is the difference between a two-minute diagnosis and another bisect, and it is the part of this PR I would protect hardest in review.

**Documented search:** I looked for three things and found no concern — that the withheld-tab assertion targets a *different* tab than the focused one (it does: `stage.node` is the pre-`addItem` two-item node, so `items.find(id => id !== activeId)` is the original second tab, not the witness); that the focus-retention assertion is not the only assertion, which would let a build that still drops the partition pass (it is not — action retention is asserted both in the poll and again per-id with a named message, which is the ticket's "the last clause is the one that matters"); and that the post-narrowing outcome object cannot pass vacuously (its `toEqual` demands all five flags exactly, and the earlier `beforeActions.length > 1` baseline assertion prevents a zero-action header from making retention trivial).

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit:**

- [x] PR description: matches the diff. "This PR changes only the test" is literally true — one added file, no source, no workflow, no config.
- [x] Anchor & Echo summaries: the JSDoc states what is witnessed and the exact command to run it, including the required `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`. No ticket-number anchors inside the code that would rot.
- [x] `[RETROSPECTIVE]`: not used; correct for a test-only addition.
- [x] Linked anchors: the red control cites a ticket checkpoint rather than restating it, which is the right direction for the link.

**Findings:** Pass — no drift. The CI-coverage point above is a lane property, recorded as a watch.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: none. Worth preserving for the next person who touches the overflow cap: the reason widening a *non-focused* tab cannot stage this is the joint-overflow bound from #19285 — with both ids protected the widened **active** tab wins the displacement, so the focused tab is withheld either way and the arm goes red on a correct build. In-order packing overflows the *last* tab regardless of width, so the extra width buys no survival by itself. That is a non-obvious property of the packer and it is the single most reusable fact in this ticket.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: the NL lane's absence from CI is the standing gap, not a defect introduced here — but the ticket's history (a bisect burned on a staging defect) is the concrete cost of that gap, and it is worth carrying as the justification whenever someone proposes registering these specs.
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: The arm asserts its **premises** before its conclusion — the stage is real, focus is really held (document *and* worker), the action set has really settled, the width has really changed, and an overflow has really happened before retention is judged. A test that verifies its own staging is the difference between a red build and a red test, and this one is careful enough to tell them apart.
